name: Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse)

card.summary: A prodrug of dextroamphetamine approved for ADHD and binge-eating disorder; its link to appearance is appetite and weight, and it is a Schedule II controlled stimulant.
card.note: Boxed warning for abuse, misuse and addiction; not indicated for weight loss.

quick.overview:
Lisdexamfetamine is a prescription stimulant sold as Vyvanse in the US and Elvanse in Europe. It is approved to treat ADHD in people aged 6 and over and moderate to severe binge-eating disorder (BED) in adults.

Its relevance to appearance culture comes from the BED indication and the appetite-suppressing effects of amphetamines in general. Trials in BED measured binge-eating days, not body weight as a cosmetic goal, and the US label states it is not indicated for weight loss.
quick.mechanism: The drug is inactive until red blood cells split off its lysine component, releasing dextroamphetamine. Dextroamphetamine raises norepinephrine and dopamine signalling. The US label says the exact way it works in ADHD and BED is not known.
quick.risks: It is a Schedule II controlled substance in the US with a boxed warning for abuse, misuse and addiction. The label also warns of cardiovascular risks, raised blood pressure and heart rate, and psychiatric reactions such as mania or psychosis, and it is contraindicated with MAO inhibitors. It requires a prescription.

lead: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate, marketed as Vyvanse in the United States and Elvanse in Europe, is a central nervous system stimulant and a prodrug of dextroamphetamine. It is formed by attaching the amino acid lysine to dextroamphetamine, and the active drug is released after enzymatic hydrolysis in the bloodstream [1][2]. It is prescribed for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children aged 6 and older and adults, and for moderate to severe binge-eating disorder (BED) in adults [2].

Lisdexamfetamine appears in appearance-related discussion because of its use in BED and because amphetamines reduce appetite. Controlled trials have tested it as a treatment for BED, with reduction in binge-eating days as the main outcome [3]. The US drug label does not list weight loss as an indication [2].

The drug carries a boxed warning in the US for abuse, misuse and addiction [2]. Systematic reviews of ADHD medications have compared amphetamines including lisdexamfetamine with other drug classes for efficacy and tolerability [4]. No published trial has tested it for cosmetic or looksmaxxing goals.

paras: The US label lists two indications: ADHD in patients aged 6 years and older, and moderate to severe binge-eating disorder in adults [2]. Grokipedia reports that the FDA first approved it in 2007 for children with ADHD and extended the approval to adults in 2008 [1].

In a tolerance and efficacy trial, adults with ADHD taking lisdexamfetamine had greater symptom improvement than those taking placebo [5]. Phase III pediatric trials in children aged 6 to 12 reported similar findings for ADHD symptom scores [6][7].

Amphetamines suppress appetite, and decreased appetite and weight loss are recognised effects of the class. The BED indication is a psychiatric one, and the US label says lisdexamfetamine is not indicated for weight loss. Binge-eating disorder is associated with overweight, obesity and metabolic comorbidities [8]. No published trial has tested lisdexamfetamine for cosmetic weight loss or other appearance goals in people without BED or ADHD.

Lisdexamfetamine is pharmacologically inactive until it is converted to dextroamphetamine. Grokipedia describes this as hydrolysis by red blood cells that limits how fast the active drug appears [1]. Amphetamines are sympathomimetic amines that raise extracellular norepinephrine and dopamine, according to general pharmacology reviews [9]. The US label states that the exact mode of therapeutic action in ADHD and BED is not known [2].

Grokipedia reports that dextroamphetamine levels peak around 3.5 hours after a dose in children and about 5 hours in adults, with effects lasting roughly 12 to 14 hours [1]. It also reports that the prodrug design produced lower drug-liking scores than immediate-release dextroamphetamine in human abuse-liability studies [1]. The US label nonetheless warns that misuse, including by non-oral routes, can cause overdose and death [2].

The boxed warning states that lisdexamfetamine has a high potential for abuse and misuse that can lead to a substance use disorder, including addiction, and that misuse of CNS stimulants can result in overdose and death [2].

Warnings and precautions in the label include risks in patients with serious cardiac disease, increased blood pressure and heart rate, and psychiatric adverse reactions. Prescribers are advised to screen for risk factors for mania and to consider stopping the drug if new psychotic or manic symptoms appear [2]. Use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors can cause hypertensive crisis and is contraindicated [2]. Grokipedia also lists growth suppression in children among the monitored effects [1].

On pregnancy, the label states that available human data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk of birth defects or miscarriage, while noting that adverse outcomes such as premature delivery and low birth weight have been seen in infants of mothers dependent on amphetamines [2].

Lisdexamfetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance in the United States and requires a prescription [1][2]. Generic versions are available, and bioequivalence trials of generic capsules against the branded product (marketed as Elvanse in Europe) have been registered [10].

The sources reviewed contain no substantial documentation of how looksmaxxing forums discuss the drug. Its inclusion in the wiki reflects its binge-eating indication and the general appetite-suppressing effect of stimulants.

A randomized clinical trial in adults with moderate to severe BED, published in JAMA Psychiatry in 2015, tested lisdexamfetamine against placebo and reported fewer binge-eating days at higher dose arms [11]. A 2019 meta-analysis of psychological and medical treatments for BED compared drug and therapy effects on binge frequency [12]. A 2022 meta-review of eating disorder treatment meta-analyses also covered this evidence base [13].

A 2018 network meta-analysis of randomized trials in The Lancet Psychiatry compared oral ADHD medications in children, adolescents and adults and examined efficacy and tolerability [4]. Registered pediatric and adult trials include a phase III study in 297 children aged 6 to 12 [7] and a 2008 placebo-controlled adult study [5].

Smaller trials have examined lisdexamfetamine in bulimia nervosa (a terminated phase 2 study) [14], cocaine dependence (a terminated pilot) [15], and residual symptoms and cognitive impairment in major depressive disorder [16]. A phase 4 study examined its cardiovascular effects in adults with ADHD, including hypertensive participants [17], and another looked at its pharmacokinetics after bariatric surgery [18]. These are not approved uses.

timeline.event: FDA approves lisdexamfetamine for ADHD in children aged 6 to 12 [1].
Approval extended to adults with ADHD [1].
JAMA Psychiatry publishes a randomized trial in adults with moderate to severe binge-eating disorder [11].
